item.title: Phase control of interfering stimulated Raman pathways in the XUV regime
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02024-9 Researchers modulate population transfer from the helium ground state to a metastable state by controlling the relative phase between two interfering stimulated Raman pathways through the continuum, demonstrating phase-coherent control in the extreme ultraviolet.

item.title: Stable deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes with reduced efficiency roll-off via accelerated exciton utilization
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02029-4 Deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes leveraging phosphor-assisted TADF-sensitized fluorescence enable accelerated exciton dynamics, resulting in devices with an external quantum efficiency of 35.9% and an LT80 lifetime of 632 h.

item.title: Perovskite chiral multiple quantum wells with extended spin lifetime via efficient spin cascade
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 15 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02027-6 Chiral multiple quantum wells enhance spin coherence in perovskites through spin cascade, achieving over 5-ns spin lifetime at room temperature.

item.title: Strong coupling of photon to an electron on helium
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02018-7 Strong coupling of photon to an electron on helium

item.title: Nonlinear circular dichroism reveals the local Berry curvature
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02025-8 The nonlinear high harmonic circular dichroism for crystals with broken time-reversal symmetry is found to be directly proportional to the local Berry curvature, and it can be directly probed via ultrafast all-optical measurements.

item.title: A new way to detect stabilizing properties of optical devices
item.description: In optical fibers, chips and other light-guiding devices, minor defects can scatter photons and disrupt their path. A new study demonstrates a way to reveal properties which, in certain systems, help light wave behavior withstand such flaws. The method could help speed up the search for new kinds of electronics and optical technologies, and contribute to more reliable quantum devices.

item.title: Physicists prove a long-suspected quantum speed limit for thermalization
item.description: Whether we are waiting for a car windshield to defrost in winter or a warm drink to cool down, how long it takes for an object to settle into a stable, even temperature within its environment (thermal equilibrium) depends on numerous factors. These can include surface area, the material properties of an object and airflow.

item.title: New high-frequency method boosts 2D material readout for next-gen quantum computers
item.description: Quantum computers represent a next step in the fast-paced evolution of technology. Using quantum bits (qubits), they have the potential to run certain calculations exponentially faster than conventional computers. However, developing and fine-tuning quantum computers requires an enormous number of repetitive tests. To accelerate quantum technology development, we need a method that can read quantum states at ultrafast speeds.

item.title: Even or odd numbers: A single molecule makes all the difference in the quantum world
item.description: The researchers in the Quantum Detection Microscopy group at CIC nanoGUNE, in collaboration with chemists at CiQUS of the University of Santiago de Compostela, have demonstrated that adding or removing a single molecule from a quantum chain can fundamentally change its interaction with a superconductor.

item.title: Using quantum entanglement to probe hidden properties of quarks
item.description: Researchers propose a new way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model by studying quantum-entangled quark pairs produced in electron-positron collisions The post Using quantum entanglement to probe hidden properties of quarks appeared first on Physics World .

item.description: Cirac is honoured for contributions to modern quantum information science The post Quantum physicist Ignacio Cirac awarded 2026 Isaac Newton Medal and Prize appeared first on Physics World .

item.title: Engineering the unknown: building vacuum and cryogenic systems for the quantum frontier
item.description: Qubit decoherence remains the primary barrier to many practical quantum devices. This is why vacuum and cryogenic equipment scaling are key enablers to delivering useful quantum products and systems The post Engineering the unknown: building vacuum and cryogenic systems for the quantum frontier appeared first on Physics World .

item.title: Sound waves come in quantum jumps
item.description: First observation of fundamental quantization in mechanical vibrations could have applications in quantum error correction and protein diagnostics The post Sound waves come in quantum jumps appeared first on Physics World .

item.title: New monolithic ion trap opens quantum simulations to more researchers
item.description: Some quantum systems are so complex that even the most powerful supercomputers struggle to simulate their behavior. One solution is quantum simulation: building a controllable quantum system in the lab and tuning it to mimic the one researchers want to understand.

item.title: Quantum magic state cleanup cuts errors 40-fold in first successful hardware test
item.description: Qubits, the quantum equivalent of digital bits, are fragile and prone to errors. That makes building reliable quantum computers extremely difficult. One fix has been to use traditional magic state distillation, which filters out flaws, but it is extremely resource-intensive.

item.title: Faster cryogenics speeds up quantum testing
item.description: A cryostat that can reach temperatures of 4 K and warm back up again within just two hours offers an efficient solution for testing the electronic components needed to build quantum computers The post Faster cryogenics speeds up quantum testing appeared first on Physics World .

item.title: Maxwell's demon learns to turn concealed information into usable energy for microscopic systems
item.description: Since its introduction more than 150 years ago, the thought-provoking idea of Maxwell's demon has profoundly shaped our understanding of the relationship between information and energy. Maxwell's demon is an imagined microscopic gatekeeper that exploits information at the microscopic scale to produce macroscopic work.

item.title: Quantum calculations reveal how spin defects lose energy
item.description: When light hits a tiny defect embedded in a solid material like diamond or silicon carbide, it can kick the defect's electrons into an excited state. These spin defects have the potential to be used as stable, readable qubits for quantum technologies, for example, quantum sensing. But modeling the full physics of their energetics over time—a key step in developing spin defects into new technologies—is a challenging task.

item.title: Your beer can only cool so fast. Blame quantum mechanics
item.description: New study places a quantum limit on how fast a system can reach a state of thermal equilibrium The post Your beer can only cool so fast. Blame quantum mechanics appeared first on Physics World .

item.title: IBM executive warns of risk of quantum computing hacks
item.description: Organizations are unprepared for the risks posed by quantum computing, IBM's Europe and Africa vice president Alessandro Curioni told AFP Wednesday, referring to the high-speed technology that could crack security encryptions and enable large-scale cyberattacks.

item.title: Software advance brings complex quantum simulations to standard computers
item.description: A major software advance could aid the creation of bigger, more reliable quantum computers, a study suggests. Researchers have developed an algorithm that enables off-the-shelf computers to run quantum simulations previously only possible using the world's most powerful supercomputers.

item.title: From spin wave to superconducting circuit: A one-way street for quantum information
item.description: Quantum information systems could one day shape everyday life through faster computing, sharper sensing and more secure communication. A new result from the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (U. of I.) marks an important step toward enabling magnetic spins—a quantum property of matter that can be used to store and manipulate information—to play a role in the future of quantum information processing.

item.title: Jamming the flow to enable memory in quantum materials
item.description: Understanding and controlling phase transitions are fundamental to physics and central to many technological revolutions. There is currently strong interest in materials with coupled structural and electronic phase transitions, where controlling the transition plasticity naturally yields built-in memory—a key step in emulating neurons and synapses for "neuromorphic" or brain-like computing technologies.

item.description: 昨日，科技部、金融监管总局、工业和信息化部、国家知识产权局联合印发《关于加快推动科技保险高质量发展 有力支撑高水平科技自立自强的若干意见》（以下简称《意见》），旨在健全重大技术攻关风险分散机制，构建覆盖科技创新全链条、全周期的科技保险政策体系。

item.title: 工信部召开务虚会 研究谋划“十五五”及开局之年工作：以综合整治“内卷式”竞争为重点
item.description: 2025年12月7日，工业和信息化部党组书记、部长李乐成主持召开务虚会，深入学习贯彻党的二十届四中全会精神，研究谋划“十五五”及开局之年工作思路和举措。部领导辛国斌、叶民、张云明、熊继军、柯吉欣、单忠德、谢远生、张建民、高东升、谢少锋、钟志红出席会议，结合分管领域工作逐一发言，交流学习体会，分析研判当前形势，提出意见建议。

item.title: 工信部筹建量子信息标准化技术委员会
